answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a saffron as the anchor of the cost.
